Description:
Vehicles abandoned in a private property may be reported to Customer Service of Urban Environment Sector.

Vehicles abandoned may be reported to the Customer Service of Urban Environment Sector tel. 09 8162 5100 Monday to Friday.  

Abandoned vehicles will be transferred to the vehicle depot of the city. If the vehicle has burnt up or it is a danger to the environment or people, the city will tow the vehicle directly to a treatment facility.
Short Description: Vehicles abandoned in a private property may be reported to Customer Service of Urban Environment Sector.
Other Links: Urban Environment Customer Service: https://www.espoo.fi/en/units/63749
Mini Description: This service lets residents report abandoned vehicles on private property to the Urban Environment Sector, which will arrange removal by transferring the vehicle to the city depot or towing it to a treatment facility if it is burnt or hazardous.

Service Name: Abandoned vehicles in the area of a property
Description:
The city may move a vehicle abandoned in a private area. 

A property owner may report a car parked in the area of the property to the Urban Environment Customer Service. A vehicle parked incorrectly on private property can be towed upon a justified request by the landowner or holder.

Call Urban Environment Customer Service: 09 8162 5100 Mon-Fri 10-15.30 or send an e-mail: asy@espoo.fi
Short Description: The city may move a vehicle abandoned in a private area.
Other Links: Urban Environment Customer Service: https://www.espoo.fi/en/units/63749
Mini Description: Property owners can report abandoned or improperly parked vehicles on private property to the Urban Environment Customer Service, and the city may tow them upon a justified request.

Description:
The new detailed plan may change street names. The new names will be adopted as the implementation of the detailed plan progresses in the area. Landowners will be informed in writing of any changes in the street name or address number. The city will also inform the postal service, the Digital and Population Data Services Agency and the Rescue Department about the address change.  

When the new address enters into force, the owner/holder of the built plot must place the address number plate in a place on the plot from where it is clearly visible from the street.
 
Address enquiries email: osoitenumerointi@espoo.fi
Short Description: The new detailed plan may change street names. The new names will be adopted as the implementation of the detailed plan progresses in the area.
Other Links: City Surveying services: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/21972
Mini Description: This service manages updates to street names and property address numbers as part of a detailed city plan, informs landowners and authorities of changes, and requires the new address numbers to be clearly displayed.

Description:
The city has both long-term and short-term contracts with companies that advertise in street areas. The advertisements are mostly at bus stops and lamp posts.    

Temporary advertisement spots 
Bridge rails and other structures that do not compromise traffic or general safety as well as public areas can be rented as advertising spots for up to two weeks.        

Bridge banners
It is possible to apply for a temporary advertising permit (also for commercial purposes) for bridge railings (13 locations) for up to two weeks. Political advertisements on bridge banners are not permitted. Advertising spots are available on the railings of the following bridges:

1 Lintulaaksontie northern/ Lintulaaksonsilta bridge
2 Lintulaaksontie southern/ Pikkulinnunsilta bridge
3 Viherlaaksontie/Shopping centre
4 Espoonväylä/Kiltakuja
5 Merituulentie/Koulusilta bridge
6 Nöykkiönkatu/Vehaksensilta bridge
7 Olarinkatu/Meteorinranta
8 Kuitinmäentie/Piispansilta bridge
9 Martinsillantie/Tukkurinsilta bridge
10 Matinkatu/Shopping centre
11 Soukantie/Shopping centre
12 Soukantie/Kastevuorenraitti
13 Alakartanontie/Kastevuorenkuja

The advertiser is responsible for commissioning the bridge banners and installing them.

Prices of temporary advertisements
A. No fee is charged for advertising events for the public good. These include:

Events for the public good that are open to all, free of charge, and organized by the city, organizations, associations, educational institutes, and day-care centers
time slots of sports clubs and organizations in park fields
granting small-scale, temporary traffic arrangements due to family events and similar if they do not cause a need for inspection visits
cleaning and environmental work parties
events related to general elections during the election advertisement period
work, exercises, or events of the defense forces, police or rescue department, etc.
research and work projects of the ministries and state-owned institutions
work related to the city's units
an ice cream van or similar mobile sales stand or point making a quick stop in the area
B. Community advertisements: €15 + VAT (24%)/day (sporting events, cultural events)

C. Business advertisements: €60 + VAT (24%)/day

Event signage
A permit can be applied for the signage of an event (e.g. a sporting or cultural event, shop opening, or some other similar public event or celebration). The maximum number of advertisements awarded for one permit application is 30 and they are meant to be placed within a restricted area (e.g. city district) to serve as signage for a single event. 

An event signage permit costs €60 + VAT (24%)/2 days. The city monitors the appropriateness of the advertisements and is entitled to remove unauthorised advertisements from the street areas and to charge for the resulting costs.

Apply for a permit electronically via the Electronic services for construction and land use (in Finnish). You can find the correct permit application under Yleisten alueiden luvat (public area permits) in Mainoslupa (advertisement permit).
Short Description: The city has both long-term and short-term contracts with companies that advertise in street areas. The advertisements are mostly at bus stops and lamp posts.
Other Links: Urban Environment Customer Service: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/63749
Mini Description: This service provides permits and manages street-area advertising (temporary and event-based) at locations such as bus stops and bridge railings, with defined pricing and an online application process.

Description:
By registering yourself as a jobseeker, you become a customer of the employment services and you can start job seeking.


You will receive job search counselling and guidance when you register as a jobseeker in the employment services of your region. As a jobseeker, you can apply for unemployment benefit from Kela or your unemployment fund. The employment authority issues a statement on the matter to Kela or the unemployment fund.

The employment authority will advise and guide you in applying for work and selecting the right services. Your employment will be supported through an initial interview, an employment plan and job search discussions.

Once you have registered as a jobseeker, the employment authority will arrange an initial interview with you within five working days. In the interview, you and an expert will discuss what kind of jobs you could apply for or whether you need to acquire training or change fields. The employment authority will also draw up an employment plan with you.

During job search discussions, you will be in regular contact with the employment authority in your area. Between the discussions, you apply for work independently or participate in services promoting employment in accordance with the employment plan.
Short Description: By registering yourself as a jobseeker, you become a customer of the employment services and you can start job seeking.

Mini Description: This service provides registered jobseekers with personalized counselling, an employment plan, and ongoing support to find work and manage unemployment benefit applications.

Service Name: Afternoon activities and care for pupils
Description:
Espoo organises afternoon activities for pupils in grades 1-2 and for pupils requiring special support after the school day.

Espoo organises afternoon activities for pupils in grades 1-2 and for pupils requiring learning and school attendance support after the school day. Afternoon group activities in schools are organised by schools, organisations and private service providers. Afternoon activities are recreational activities organized in groups of 15 children, where one adult supervises the group. In addition to guided activities, the children can focus on their own playing. The afternoons are spent both indoors and outdoors. The children participating in the afternoon activities are insured and covered by the personal accident insurance of the city. Afternoon activities of basic education are subject to a fee. Based on the income of the family, it is possible to apply for a payment relief or remission for the service. Applying for afternoon activities of schools is done for one school year at a time. Activities are not organised during school holidays or school Saturdays. Afternoon activities of basic education are organised in 62 locations.
Short Description: Espoo organises afternoon activities for pupils in grades 1-2 and for pupils requiring special support after the school day.

Service Name: Applying for construction and operation permissions
Description:
The Espoo Building Control Department grants the permissions needed for construction and renovation of buildings and structures. Building Control also grants permissions for landscape work and demolition. It is recommended to apply for the permissions through electronic customer service. Building Control organises pre-negotiations before applying for the permission.

Construction generally requires a building permit or another approval by an authority. The extension of a building, significant repairs and alterations and a change of purpose also require a building or operation permit. The issue is stipulated in the Land Use and Building Act. The municipality's Building Code may also define which operations are subject to permission or declaration.

The qualification of the designers of a construction project is stipulated by law. The permission procedure also includes notifying the neighbours and/or obtaining their permission. Construction may not be started until the permission decision is legally valid.
Short Description: The Espoo Building Control Department grants the permissions needed for construction and renovation of buildings and structures. Building Control also grants permissions for landscape work and demolition. It is recommended to apply for the permissions through electronic customer service. Building Control organises pre-negotiations before applying for the permission.
Other Links: Espoo Building Control: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/21970
Mini Description: This service handles applications and approvals for construction, renovation, demolition, and landscape work, including pre-negotiations and neighbour notification, and ensures the permit is legally valid before work can begin.

Service Name: Applying for exemption from wastewater system renovation
Description: You can apply for an exemption from the deadline for renovating your property-specific wastewater system. An exemption only needs to be applied for if the system does not comply with the requirements of the Environmental Protection Act and the building is located less than 100 metres from a water system or in an important groundwater area. In other areas, there is no need to renovate the wastewater system until a flush toilet is built or a full renovation is made.
Short Description: You can apply for an exemption from the deadline for renovating your property-specific wastewater system.
Other Links: Environmental protection services: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/66794; Environmental supervision: https://www.espoo.fi/fi/asuminen-ja-rakentaminen/ymparistonsuojelu/ymparistovalvonta/ymparistovalvonnan-luvat-ilmoitukset-ja-rekisterointi#section-15217
Mini Description: This service lets property owners apply for an exemption from wastewater system renovation deadlines when the system is non-compliant and the building is within 100 meters of a water system or in an important groundwater area; in other areas, renovation can be postponed until a flush toilet is installed or a full renovation is carried out.

Description:
Researchers at the City Museum are happy to answer your questions about the history of Espoo. You can send your question to kaupunginmuseo(at)espoo.fi

What was there in the area of Espoo 6,000 years ago? Where was the oldest manor in Espoo located? What is the story of Mankby? Where was the Espoo hypermarket located? Researchers at the City Museum are happy to answer your questions about the history of Espoo. You can send your own question, or you can explore the history of Espoo at the exhibition A Thousand Stories about Espoo.

The information search for brief questions is free. Wider questions are separately negotiated.
Short Description: Researchers at the City Museum are happy to answer your questions about the history of Espoo. You can send your question to kaupunginmuseo(at)espoo.fi
Other Links: KAMU Espoo City Museum: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/20405
Mini Description: Ask the museum is a service where City Museum researchers answer questions about Espoo's history by email, with free brief inquiries and negotiated terms for broader questions, plus access to the "A Thousand Stories about Espoo" exhibition.

Description:
Through its audience outreach work, the Tapiola Sinfonietta provides musical encounters and experiences free of charge for people not reached by the orchestra's public concerts. This work addresses all age groups and social groups. 
Small ensembles of the Tapiola Sinfonietta perform at dozens of public venues of the City of Espoo each year, such as child care clinics, schools and hospitals. There are also interactive concerts for the orchestra's 'godchildren' and for schoolchildren. 
Concerts organised along the KULPS! Culture and Sports Path reach schoolchildren in grades 1 to 9 at Espoo schools every year. The orchestra is also involved in services of the City of Espoo such as the Culture Clinic, the Culture Chain and Culture Buddy programmes, and in the national Echo Card service.
The Tapiola Sinfonietta performs at city events in Espoo, and public events free of charge are often held in connection with concerts.
Seven of the members of the orchestra have trained as hospital musicians, and our community musician works with special needs groups and the elderly.
Short Description: Small ensembles of the Tapiola Sinfonietta perform at dozens of public venues of the City of Espoo each year, such as child care clinics, schools and hospitals. There are also interactive concerts for the orchestra's 'godchildren' and for schoolchildren.

Mini Description: Audience Outreach Work delivers free, accessible musical encounters to diverse Espoo communities by performing small-ensemble and interactive concerts at clinics, schools, hospitals, and public venues, reaching audiences not served by the orchestra’s regular concerts.

Cadastral procedures include parcelling of a plot, easement proceedings, definition of real estate (e.g. demarcation), parcelling of a public area or space as well as redemption of a parcel or exchange of land in conjunction with the parcelling.

Espoo's carpet washing sites are available to all Espoo residents during summertime.

During summertime, Espoo´s seven carpet washing sites are available to all residents free of charge.

All carpet washing sites have carpet washing basins of different sizes, wringers, drying racks, and a table and chairs or a bench. 

The water comes to the washing sites from the municipal water supply network, and the wastewater is conveyed into the municipal sewer network. 

The most environmentally friendly way to wash carpets is at a designated site equipped with sewers. It is prohibited to clean carpets in the sea, lakes, or other bodies of water. The same applies to dry land if the washing water ends in a body or a ditch. Washing carpets in the sea and lakes harms the environment and causes, for example, clouding of water and overgrowth of algae. 

Remember to clean up after using the washing site: close the taps and put your litter in the bin. This makes carpet washing more pleasant for everyone and helps to keep carpet washing sites operational throughout the summer.

Carpet washing sites are intended for carpet washing only and are open in weeks 18-39, depending on weather conditions.
Short Description: Espoo's carpet washing sites are available to all Espoo residents during summertime.

Service Name: Certificate for a partially disabled jobseeker
Description:
If you have a disability or illness affecting work, you can request a certificate for a partially disabled jobseeker from the Employment services.

If you have an injury or illness diagnosed by a physician that affects your employment and you are about to be employed by a large employer, you can ask the Employment services for a certificate stating that you have been registered as partially disabled in the Employment services' customer information system. A large employer is an employer who has insurance from an employment pension company and whose annual salary exceeds the large employer's salary limit.

A certificate of a partially disabled jobseeker reduces the threshold for a large employer to hire an employee with partial work ability and promotes your employment. When you have the certificate, your employer's employment pension contribution category will not change if you have to retire on a disability pension during the first five years of your employment relationship.
Short Description: If you have a disability or illness affecting work, you can request a certificate for a partially disabled jobseeker from the Employment services.
Other Links: Espoo Employment Services, office in Sello: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/76109; Espoo Employment Services, Piispanportti office: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/63889
Mini Description: This service lets a partially disabled jobseeker obtain a certificate from Employment Services (registered in the customer information system) that lowers large employers’ hiring threshold for partially able workers and preserves the employee’s pension contribution category for the first five years of employment if disability retirement occurs.

Service Name: Demolition permit and notice of demolition
Description:
A demolition permit is required for the demolition of a building or part thereof. A permit is not required for the demolition of an outbuilding and any similar minor building, unless the building is considered to be of historical significance, architectural value or part of such an entity. Unless a permit is required for the demolition of the building or part thereof, a written notice of demolition must be submitted.  

A building or part of a building may not be demolished without a permit in a town plan area or in an area where there is a building prohibition referred to in Section 53 of the Land Use and Building Act in force to prepare a town plan. A permit is also required if the master plan so dictates. A demolition permit is subject to the condition that the demolition does not entail the destruction of heritage, beauty or other values contained in the built environment and does not impede the realisation of land use planning.
Short Description: A demolition permit is required for the demolition of a building or part thereof. A permit is not required for the demolition of an outbuilding and any similar minor building, unless the building is considered to be of historical significance, architectural value or part of such an entity. Unless a permit is required for the demolition of the building or part thereof, a written notice of demolition must be submitted.

Description:
You may receive discretionary expense allowance if you incur costs for participating in a service.

Employment services may grant you discretionary expense allowance when you participate in a service that supports your employment as agreed in your employment plan or a plan replacing it. You can receive compensation from the Employment services if you incur inevitable costs for participating in a service and you do not receive unemployment security from Kela or an unemployment fund.

Expense allowance can be paid for your participation in
- labour market training
- work trial
- training trial
- career coaching
- job search coaching
- independent study as an integration client.

Expense allowance is usually nine euros per day. You can receive expense allowance for up to five days a week and only for those days when you participate in the agreed service. Expense allowance is not paid for holidays or absences, for example.

The expense allowance is 18 euros a day if the service is provided outside your labour market region. The expense allowance will also be 18 euros when the service is provided outside Espoo and you have accommodation expenses.
Short Description: You may receive discretionary expense allowance if you incur costs for participating in a service.

Service Name: Disposal of waste in the ground, notification
Description:
The Environment and Building Control Department must be contacted about the use of waste in excavation or other disposal of waste in the ground before starting the activity.

The holder of a property must notify the Environment and Building Control Department in writing about the disposal of waste other than garden waste and composted food or lavatory waste in the ground, unless the disposal requires an environmental permit or another statutory notification because of the amount of waste. The notification must be made at least 30 days before the disposal of the waste. The notification must be appended with any analysis results describing the environmental acceptability of the waste, a map drawing of the disposal site and an account of how the waste is to be placed in the ground.

A person planning the disposal of waste in the ground should be in contact with the Environment and Building Control Department well before starting the operation.
Short Description: The Environment and Building Control Department must be contacted about the use of waste in excavation or other disposal of waste in the ground before starting the activity.

Description:
A permanent right of use, i.e. an easement, may be established to benefit a plot in the area of another plot. An easement established in this procedure remains valid even if the plot owners change.  

The most common easements are road easements and various types of easements regarding water and sewerage pipes, power cables, etc., and easements established for keeping cars. An easement may also be established for a waste collection place. Easements are established at the request of the owner in connection with the parcelling procedure or in a separate easement survey, and their establishment usually requires an easement agreement between the plot owners. The application can be submitted either through the electronic service (online application) or by sending it by post. 

The establishment of an easement in connection with plot parcelling costs €130 per easement. A separate easement survey, establishing 1 easement, costs €500. The cost of each subsequent easement is €130. The easement survey takes approximately 1-2 months. In urgent cases, the applicant can speed up the process by obtaining written acceptance for it from all parties.
Short Description: A permanent right of use, i.e. an easement, may be established to benefit a plot in the area of another plot. An easement established in this procedure remains valid even if the plot owners change.

Service Name: Employment subsidy for people aged 55 or over
Description:
The employment subsidy is a financial subsidy for employers for the salary costs of an unemployed jobseeker aged 55 or over.

The employment subsidy is a benefit intended to promote the employment of unemployed jobseekers aged 55 or over that an employment authority can grant to an employer to cover pay costs. The purpose of the subsidy is to promote the employment of people aged 55 or over by improving their professional skills or entrepreneurial skills. The subsidy is granted and paid to the employer, but its granting is always based on the unemployed jobseeker's service need.

The employment subsidy requires that the unemployed jobseeker hired for the employment relationship has reached the age of 55 and has been unemployed for at least 24 months in the 28 months immediately preceding the granting of the subsidy.

An employment subsidy may be granted for a full-time employment contract valid until further notice or a fixed-term full-time employment contract. The person hired with the subsidy must work for the recipient for at least 25 hours a week. If the regular working hours in the sector are less than 37.5 hours per week, the working hours must be at least 65 per cent of the regular working hours in the sector.

The unemployed jobseeker's employment plan or pay subsidy card includes a mention of the subsidy.

The amount of employment subsidy is 70 per cent of the wage costs. The aid may be granted for a period of 10 months but not longer than the duration of the employment relationship. The maximum amount of employment subsidy paid is €1,770 per month. The pay covered with the subsidy is the pay subject to withholding tax that is paid to the employee on the basis of working hours or the performance of a contract.
Short Description: The employment subsidy is a financial subsidy for employers for the salary costs of an unemployed jobseeker aged 55 or over.
Other Links: Espoo Employment Services, office in Sello: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/76109; Espoo Employment Services, Piispanportti office: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/63889
Mini Description: A wage subsidy provided to employers to cover 70% of the wages for hiring unemployed jobseekers aged 55 or over, for up to 10 months (maximum €1,770 per month) to promote their employment.

Service Name: Exemption from joining the water utility's water supply or sewerage network
Description:
Exemption from joining the water utility's water supply or sewerage network can be applied for.

According to the Water Services Act, a property located in the area covered by the water utility's water supply and sewerage network must join the network. The aim is to protect the environment and human health. 

It is possible to apply for exemption from the obligation. Its granting is conditional on, among other things, circumstances that make joining the network unreasonable, the sufficient availability of high-quality domestic water and the proper treatment of wastewater. The exemption is granted on a temporary basis. 
Exemption from the obligation can be applied for from the Environment and Building Control Department. The exemption can be granted if all exemption criteria listed in the Act on Water Services are met.
Short Description: Exemption from joining the water utility's water supply or sewerage network can be applied for.

Service Name: Extended transition security for employees aged 55 or over
Description:
In the event of dismissal, those aged 55 or over may receive extended transition security services that help them to re-employ quickly.

If you are dismissed from your employment relationship on production or financial grounds and you have turned 55, you may be entitled to extended transition security. The extended transition security services will support your rapid re-employment. 

Transition security for those aged 55 or over includes
- transition security allowance,
- transition security training and
- extended employment leave of 5, 15 or 25 days. 

The transition security allowance is, on average, equal to your one-month salary. The transition security allowance is paid by the institution paying the unemployment benefit, i.e. an unemployment fund or Kela. 

The purpose of the transition security training is to promote your re-employment. The training increases your professional skills or supports your business operations, and its content meets your training needs. The training may last up to six months and is organised by the employment authority. Participating in the training is voluntary. 

Under the Employment Contracts Act, your employer must inform you if you are entitled to transition security for those aged 55 or over. The obligation to provide information applies to all employers.
Short Description: In the event of dismissal, those aged 55 or over may receive extended transition security services that help them to re-employ quickly.
Other Links: Espoo Employment Services, office in Sello: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/76109; Espoo Employment Services, Piispanportti office: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/63889
Mini Description: Extended transition security for employees aged 55 or over provides financial support (about one month’s salary), transition training, and extended paid leave to help them re-enter employment quickly after dismissal on production or financial grounds.

Espoo has more than 90 ice rinks. 

Freezing one middle-sized ice rink requires about 120 cubic metres of water when freezing begins from zero. Under optimal conditions, freezing a rink takes almost a week. Conditions are ideal when the temperature is 5 to 10 degrees Celsius below zero. If the temperature is too low, more than 20 degrees Celsius below zero, the ice begins to crack. The ice rink stays in good condition as long as the temperature stays below freezing point. As soon as the temperature rises above zero degrees Celsius, the ice starts to soften.

On the website ulkoliikunta.fi you can find information about the condition of ice rinks, when the ice rinks have been maintained, if there are changing rooms by the rink and also the opening hours of artificial rinks.

Ice skating at your own risk.

Description:
As a client of employment services, you can receive unemployment security for studying.

Independent studies with unemployment benefit means that you can complete full-time studies at an educational institution as a client of employment services. Sometimes independent study can help you find work and integrate faster.

Independent study can be
 completion of comprehensive school
 preparatory education for upper secondary school
 preparatory vocational education
 qualifying studies (e.g. physicians)
 Finnish or Swedish language studies.

The studies must be in Finnish or Swedish. If the studies are included in social orientation, they may be in your native language.

You can study with unemployment benefit for a maximum of 24 months. However, in the case of basic education, you can receive support for a maximum of 48 months. You must progress in your studies as agreed in the integration plan in order to receive support.
Short Description: As a client of employment services, you can receive unemployment security for studying.

Service Name: Instruction preparing for general upper secondary education for immigrants and foreign-language speakers
Description:
Young people with an immigrant background whose language skills are not yet sufficient for general upper secondary studies may apply for preparatory education.

Young people with an immigrant background whose language skills and other abilities are not yet sufficient for general upper secondary studies may apply for preparatory general upper secondary education. The education lasts for one school year and strengthens the students' skills in Finnish and prepares them for general upper secondary studies in a diverse way. After preparatory education, the students apply for actual general upper secondary education. 

The education can be applied for by immigrants and foreign-language-speaking young people and adults:

- who have completed basic education or an equivalent syllabus in Finland or abroad or have the equivalent knowledge and skills
- who do not have the sufficient linguistic ability to cope with upper secondary studies in Finnish or Swedish
- whose primary application preference is general upper secondary school
- who have not completed vocational upper secondary education and training or matriculation examination in Finland or equivalent education in another country.
Short Description: Young people with an immigrant background whose language skills are not yet sufficient for general upper secondary studies may apply for preparatory education.

Service Name: Job search in another EU or EEA country or Switzerland
Description:
As an unemployed jobseeker, you can go to another EU or EEA country or Switzerland to find work and receive unemployment benefits from Finland.

You can receive basic daily allowance paid by Kela or daily unemployment allowance paid by an unemployment fund from Finland. You cannot receive labour market subsidy during the trip. 

You can receive unemployment benefits in another country for a maximum of three months. In order for the benefit to be paid, the local employment authority must also accept you as a jobseeker in the country where you are looking for a job.
Short Description: As an unemployed jobseeker, you can go to another EU or EEA country or Switzerland to find work and receive unemployment benefits from Finland.

Mini Description: Allows an unemployed Finnish jobseeker to search for work in another EU/EEA country or Switzerland and receive Finnish unemployment benefits (basic daily allowance or unemployment fund allowance) for up to three months, provided the host country accepts you as a jobseeker and you do not receive labour market subsidy during the trip.

Joint procurement training is labour market training that the employment authority can organise together with the employer, the commissioner of the person intending to become an entrepreneur or the company transferring its business rights so that they participate in the funding of the training.

As an employer, you can organise labour market training to increase the professional competence and capabilities of current or future personnel. Joint procurement training may also be aimed at you as an entrepreneur when you are starting a business.

Description:
Labour market training helps you develop your professional skills and promote your employment.

Labour market training develops your professional skills and promotes your employment. Labour market training is training acquired by the Employment services. The labour authority and the educational institution providing the training plan and organise the training together. Employers can also participate in the organisation of labour market training. 

Labour market training may be:
- training that increases professional competence and capabilities
- training to increase entrepreneurial skills
- integration training.

Labour market training is free of charge, so you won't need to pay participation or examination fees. However, card and licence trainings may be subject to a fee.

If you are unemployed, you are entitled to the same unemployment security during labour market training that you get when you are unemployed. If you have agreed to labour market training in your employment plan or another plan replacing it, your unemployment security can be increased. This will be decided by the party paying the unemployment security - that is, by the unemployment fund or Kela.

If the costs of participating in the training are incurred, you can receive expense allowance for the days of participation. If you do not receive expense allowance from the party paying the unemployment benefit, that is, the unemployment fund or Kela, you can apply for discretionary expense allowance from the Employment services in Espoo.
Short Description: Labour market training helps you develop your professional skills and promote your employment.
Other Links: Espoo Employment Services, office in Sello: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/76109; Espoo Employment Services, Piispanportti office: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/63889
Mini Description: Labour market training provides free programs organized by Employment Services to develop professional and entrepreneurial skills and improve employment prospects, with unemployment security maintained during training and possible expense allowances.

Description:
Deviating from the regulations of the valid town plan is subject to a deviation permit, which must be obtained before applying for a building permit. In Espoo, all areas that are not covered by the town plan are considered areas requiring planning. Construction work in these areas is subject to a separate decision and/or deviation permit, which must be obtained before applying for a building permit. As a rule, the city's permission is required for dividing or splitting a property outside the town plan that is designated as a construction site (parcelling permit).

Deviating from the regulations of the valid town plan is subject to a deviation permit, which must be obtained before applying for a building permit. A slight deviation to be resolved in connection with the building permission procedure is defined by the building inspection authority. Sometimes deviating from the regulations of the town plan requires changing the town plan. Before submitting an application for deviating from the town plan, contact the town plan designer/engineer of the planning area at the City Planning Department or the Building Control permit drafter. In Espoo, all areas that are not covered by the town plan are considered areas requiring planning. Construction work in these areas is subject to a separate decision and/or deviation permit, which must be obtained before applying for a building permit. Deviating from the rules, regulations, prohibitions and other restrictions stipulated in the Land Use and Building Act or adopted thereunder (for example, the regulations of the building code) is subject to a deviation permit. As a rule, the city's permission, resolved in the City Planning Department, is required for dividing or splitting a property outside the town plan that is designated as a construction site. If the property is located in the town plan area, the parcelling of a plot is carried out, after the preparation of binding subdivision, by the Espoo Public Works Department city survey, from which the parcelling is applied for with a cadastral procedure application.

Description:
Maternity and child health clinics provide preventive and health-enhancing services. The services are voluntary and free of charge for families.

The purpose of maternity clinics is to support and protect the health of pregnant women and their unborn children. 

Together with the clinic staff, families get to discuss their health habits and other issues and questions they wish to bring up. It is also important to discuss difficult issues that burden a family, as this will make it possible to plan the required help and support measures as soon as possible together with the family and other cooperation partners.

Description:
The city may tow a vehicle parked incorrectly or hindering work performed on the street.

A car parked incorrectly may be reported to the Urban Environment Customer Service. 

A vehicle parked incorrectly may be transferred to the vehicle depot of the city two days after the incorrect parking was observed. 

A vehicle that prevents street work or maintenance will be towed by the city to the closest place suitable for this purpose after two days following the prompt to remove the vehicle. 

The city may immediately tow a vehicle that is considerably hindering traffic.
Short Description: The city may tow a vehicle parked incorrectly or hindering work performed on the street.
Other Links: Urban Environment Customer Service: https://www.espoo.fi/en/units/63749
Mini Description: This service allows reporting of illegally parked or obstructive vehicles, which the city may tow to a depot or other suitable location after two days, or tow immediately if the vehicle severely blocks traffic.

Description:
Espoo info service advisors also bring advisory services and digital support directly to those in need. The mobile service is a customer-oriented and agile way to bring advisory services to where the residents are. We especially aim to reach those for whom it is difficult to travel to the fixed service points of Espoo info.

Mobile Espoo info visits various places around Espoo, including service centers, community houses, and libraries. The Lippulaiva library in Espoonlahti and the Entresse library in Espoon keskus are regular locations where we are present twice a week. You can often find us at events as well; we participate in events such as Homeless Night and Espoo Day.

You can find all the visit locations and times of Mobile Espoo info in the Espoo city event calendar. If you need help with online transactions or using a smart device, you can also book an appointment for personal digital support from Espoo info. Our service advisors are happy to help you!
Short Description: Espoo info service advisors also bring advisory services and digital support directly to those in need.
Other Links: N/A
Mini Description: Mobile Espoo info provides on-site advisory services and digital support by visiting locations around Espoo—including regular visits to Lippulaiva and Entresse libraries—and events, to reach residents who cannot travel to fixed service points, with the option to book personal digital support.

Description:
If you need a comprehensive service to support your employment, you can get help from multisectoral services.

The cooperation model of multidisciplinary support that promotes employment helps you find employment if you need comprehensive support. The aim of the service is to remove obstacles to employment related to, for example, your life situation, state of health, work and functional capacity, and talents and vocational skills. 

In the cooperation model, the Employment services, wellbeing services county and Kela together with you will assess what kind of support you need for finding employment. A multisectoral employment plan will be drawn up for you. The plan will schedule the employment services, social and healthcare services and rehabilitation services you need. 

If you are under the age of 30, you can receive multisectoral advice, guidance and services meant for young people and offered jointly by different authorities and other actors at a low threshold. The purpose of the shared service of multisectoral support service promoting the employment of young people is to promote young people's study opportunities, employment, capabilities for action and wellbeing.
Short Description: If you need a comprehensive service to support your employment, you can get help from multisectoral services.

Mini Description: An integrated cross-sector service that assesses your needs and coordinates employment, health, social, and rehabilitation support to create a multisectoral plan that helps you find employment, with special low-threshold guidance for those under 30.

Service Name: Ohjaamotalo - One-Stop Guidance Centre for young people
Description:
The Ohjaamotalo One-Stop Guidance Centre is a service point for young adults under 30 years of age and living in Espoo.

Hello, all young Espoo and Kauniainen residents under the age of 30! 

More than 60 different professionals work in the Ohjaamotalo to support and guide you. Behind one door you will find help for your different needs and life situations. The Ohjaamotalo offers both individual guidance and targeted group activities.

You can get information and help from the Ohjaamotalo
- study opportunities
- working life, job search and livelihood
- housing, daily management and well-being
- leisure opportunities

At Ohjaamotalo's Starttipiste, you can get help without an appointment during opening hours. Starttipiste is open in Leppävaara on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays from 12-4 PM and at Iso Omena Service Point on Wednesdays from 12-4 PM. You can also reach us via social media, phone, or Discord. At Starttipiste, you can remain anonymous if you wish.

All our services are voluntary and free for you.
Short Description: The Ohjaamotalo One-Stop Guidance Centre is a service point for young adults under 30 years of age and living in Espoo.
Other Links: Ohjaamotalo: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/57368; Ohjaamotalo, Starttipiste in Leppävaara: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/57369; Ohjaamotalo's Starttipiste, Iso Omena Service Centre: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/59425; Ohjaamotalo: https://www.espoo.fi/en-US/Youth/Information_councelling_and_help/Ohjaamotalo
Mini Description: Ohjaamotalo is a free, one-stop guidance centre for young people under 30 in Espoo (also serving Kauniainen) that provides personalised guidance and group activities across study, work, housing and daily life, well-being, and leisure, with drop-in Starttipiste access and multiple contact options.

Description:
The Environment Department must be contacted about the handling of an underground oil tank removed from use.

According to Section 11 of the environmental protection regulations of the City of Espoo, the owner or holder of an oil, fuel or other chemical tank must remove the tank along with its pipelines from the ground and have it cleaned before its removal. 

The Environment Department may grant an exception from the obligation to remove a decommissioned oil tank from the ground, if its removal is technically very difficult or it causes damage to other property. 

The Environment Department must be contacted about leaving a tank in place as early as possible in order to assess the requirements for granting an exception.
Short Description: The Environment Department must be contacted about the handling of an underground oil tank removed from use.
Other Links: Environmental protection services: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/66794

Description:
Building sites in the detailed plan area are created by parcelling. (A binding plot subdivision must be prepared for the area before plot parcelling). Plot parcelling becomes pending at the written application of the owner or after the National Land Survey of Finland has submitted information on the title registration of a parcel to the City Survey Department. The application can be submitted either through the electronic service (online application) or by sending it by post.

The plot parcelling process takes approximately 3 months. In urgent cases, the applicant can speed up the process by obtaining written acceptance for it from all parties. The owner must have a registration of title to the real estates or parcels that form the plot.  

The plot parcelling fee depends on the size of the plot and varies between €1,100 and €1,600. If the area of an old real estate unit or plot is the same as the area of the plot according to the plot subdivision, the plot may be registered without any work in the field. The fee for the procedure is €390.
Short Description: Building sites in the detailed plan area are created by parcelling. (A binding plot subdivision must be prepared for the area before plot parcelling)

Service Name: Parcelling outside the town plan area
Description:
As a rule, the city's permission, resolved in the City Planning Department, is required for dividing or splitting a property outside the town plan that is designated as a construction site. If the property is located in the town plan area, the parcelling of a plot is carried out, after the preparation of binding subdivision, by the Espoo Public Works Department city survey, from which the parcelling is applied for with a cadastral procedure application.

As a rule, the city's permission, resolved in the City Planning Department, is required for dividing or splitting a property outside the town plan that is designated as a construction site. The general prerequisite for the city's permission is that the requirements set on the building site are met, the maximum efficiency used in the area is not exceeded and the formation of the new building site does not cause harm to the organisation of land use or the preparation or implementation of the town plan or master plan. Application forms with instructions are available at the Environment and Technical Services customer service, they can be printed from the City of Espoo website, or the application can be submitted electronically through the electronic service for construction and land use. More detailed instructions can be found on the website of the City of Espoo.
Short Description: As a rule, the city's permission, resolved in the City Planning Department, is required for dividing or splitting a property outside the town plan that is designated as a construction site. Description:
A pay subsidy is an economic benefit for employers to cover the pay of an unemployed jobseeker.


A pay subsidy is a benefit intended to promote the employment of unemployed jobseekers that an employment authority can grant to an employer to cover pay costs. The purpose of work supported by pay subsidy is to promote the employment of unemployed job seekers in the open labour market and to improve their professional competence. Pay subsidy also helps people with reduced work ability and those aged 60 or over who have been unemployed for an extended period to find work and participate in the world of work. The subsidy is granted and paid to the employer, but its granting is always based on the unemployed jobseeker's service need.

A pay subsidy may be granted for
- open-ended full-time employment
- fixed-term full-time employment
- apprenticeship training
- part-time employment if the granter of the subsidy feels that it is appropriate and that it promotes the jobseeker's possibilities to find employment.

The employment authority assesses whether the subsidy is the most appropriate means of promoting the employment of the unemployed jobseeker and decides separately the duration and amount of each support period. The unemployed jobseeker's employment plan or pay subsidy card includes a mention of the pay subsidy.

The length of the pay subsidy period depends on the duration of the person's unemployment and the impact a possibly reduced work ability might have on their work performance. Depending on the duration of the unemployment preceding the pay subsidy, the subsidy would be granted for five or ten months. The subsidy is granted for the duration of the employment relationship at most. The subsidy may be granted for hiring a long-term unemployed person aged 60 or over for a maximum of 24 months at a time.

In most cases, the amount of the pay subsidy is 50% of the salary costs incurred by the person hired with the subsidy. The amount of support granted for hiring a person with reduced work ability is 70% of their pay. The amount of support for an association, foundation or registered religious community may be 100% of the pay. The amount of subsidy granted is between 1,260 and 2,020 euros per month, depending on the grounds for granting. The pay covered with the subsidy is the pay subject to withholding tax that is paid to the employee on the basis of working hours or the performance of a contract.
Short Description: A pay subsidy is an economic benefit for employers to cover the pay of an unemployed jobseeker.

Mini Description: Pay subsidies are government wage-support payments provided to employers to cover part of an unemployed jobseeker’s wages in order to promote their employment in the open labor market, including long-term unemployed, older workers, and those with reduced work ability, across open-ended, fixed-term, apprenticeship, or part-time roles.

Description:
If the construction work subject to a building permit is not started within three years or completed within five years, the permit expires.An action permit, demolition permit or landscape work permit pires if the action is not carried out within three years. 

The time limit starts to run from the date on which the permit becomes legally valid. 

Upon separate application, the municipal Building Control authority may extend the validity of the permit for the commencement of work by a maximum of two years, provided that the legal conditions for the construction or other action are still valid. The period of validity of a permit to commence work may be extended only once. 
The time limits for completion of the work may be extended by up to three years at a time.

Service Name: Photo archive services of the City Museum
Description:
In the photo archive of the City Museum, you can study and order old photographs of Espoo by agreement.

It is easiest to browse the images in the Finna service, in which the museum has published photographs. The number is increasing all the time. Finna also includes many other things to investigate, such as documents about Espoo, maps and historical information about buildings. Photos published in Finna can be downloaded and used freely, as long as the Espoo City Museum and the name of the photographer are mentioned.

You can also come to the photo archive to study the photographs. The photo archive is located in the Espoo City Museum at Ahertajantie 5.

Description:
Place names are the basis of our address system, a vital part of the cityscape and the creator of its symbolic meanings. Various requirements and hopes are therefore placed on place names. The objective of place name planning is to attach a name to the place and the tradition. An address that stands out and is effective in use is part of the everyday life of residents.

Place name planning builds distinctive city culture and regional image without forgetting the traditional place names created by residents of Espoo throughout the centuries.

Description:
When the detailed plan has entered into force, a plot division is prepared in the area at the request of the landowner. The plot division is a block-level plan on how the block will be divided into building sites. The preparation of a plot subdivision takes approximately 2.5 months.  

A separate plot division or a change thereof is made at the written request of the owner of the area, if sufficient preconditions exist. The application can be submitted either through the electronic service (online application) or by sending it by post.

At the request of the landowner, an experimental calculation may be carried out in the city-plan area. An experimental calculation is a proposal on the kinds of building sites that can be formed in the area. The experimental calculation map can be used, for example, as an attachment map to a deed.

By registering yourself as a jobseeker, you become a customer of the employment services and you can start job seeking.

You will receive job search counselling and guidance when you register as a jobseeker in the Employment services in Espoo. As a jobseeker, you can apply for unemployment benefit from Kela or your unemployment fund. The Employment services issues a statement on the matter to Kela or the unemployment fund.

The Employment services will advise and guide you in applying for work and selecting the right services. Your employment will be supported through an initial interview, an employment plan and job search discussions.

Once you have registered as a jobseeker, the Employment services will arrange an initial interview with you within five working days. In the interview, you and your personal coach will discuss what kind of jobs you could apply for or whether you need to acquire training or change fields. The Employment services will also draw up an employment plan with you.

During job search discussions, you will be in regular contact with the Employment services in your area. Between the discussions, you apply for work independently or participate in services promoting employment in accordance with the employment plan.

Service Name: Reimbursement of travel and accommodation costs
Description:
You can get compensation for travel and accommodation costs when you are applying for a job or participating in a service that promotes employment.

You can apply for compensation for travel and accommodation costs if you are an unemployed jobseeker and
- you applying for a job
- you apply for labour market training, coaching or trial
- you participate in an expert evaluation organised by the Employment services.

You can apply for compensation for return trips made in Finland for a job interview if the work lasts at least two weeks and the average working hours are at least 18 hours. Compensation may also be granted for a job interview trip to another Member State of the European Union or to a country belonging to the European Economic Area.

To receive compensation, you must be an unemployed jobseeker. Costs may be reimbursed if:
 you participate in an admission event or aptitude test for labour market training
 you will familiarise yourself with the educational institution providing labour market training before the training begins so that you can check the accessibility and other suitability of the institution for your studies due to a disability or illness
 you visit the employment authority so that your visit is considered necessary and you need transport services due to a disability or illness
 you participate in an expert evaluation organised by the employment authority.

The basis for reimbursement of travel expenses is the distance in kilometres multiplied by €0.21. The part of the travel expenses exceeding €12 shall be reimbursed up to a maximum of €200.

Compensation is granted for accommodation expenses based on the costs incurred, up to a maximum of €80 per day.
Short Description: You can get compensation for travel and accommodation costs when you are applying for a job or participating in a service that promotes employment.
Other Links: Espoo Employment Services, office in Sello: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/76109; Espoo Employment Services, Piispanportti office: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/63889
Mini Description: Provides travel and accommodation reimbursements for unemployed jobseekers who are applying for jobs, attending labour market training or coaching, or participating in expert evaluations, with travel paid at €0.21 per kilometre up to €200 after a €12 deduction and accommodation up to €80 per day, including eligible return trips for qualifying job interviews in Finland or in EU/EEA countries.

Service Name: Renovation of external surfaces of buildings and other structures, notification
Description:
Renovation of external surfaces of buildings and other external structures requires notification to the Environment and Building Control Department.

A person renovating the external surfaces of buildings and other external structures (such as bridges or handrails) must notify the Environment and Building Control Department in writing about the renovation at least 14 days before starting the work.

The work must always be announced in advance to residents, care and educational institutions and other parties within the scope of the work that the work may cause harm or disturbance to. 

The operator must also negotiate sufficient noise and dust abatement with the sensitive parties, which the operation may unreasonably harm or disturb (for example, day-care centres and schools).

Description:
Repair grants for repairing flats of elderly and disabled people to support living at home.

The Housing Finance and Development Centre of Finland (ARA) awards repair grants from the state's funds for repairing flats of elderly and disabled people to support living at home. The Finnish Transport Agency is responsible for lighting Ring I-III, Kauklahdenväylä, Turuntie/Nupurintie, and Vihdintie.

The street lighting systems are serviced regularly, three times a year. Maintenance is carried out region by region. For cost reasons, individual bulbs are not replaced outside this schedule. Urgent faults are repaired as soon as possible.

You can report street lighting faults (burnt-out bulbs or lighting columns damaged in collisions) via Feedback Service.

Service Name: Self-motivated study subsidised with an unemployment benefit
Description:
During independent studies, you may receive unemployment benefits under certain conditions.

In some cases, you may be able to study independently while receiving the unemployment benefit. Independent studies include studies where an educational institution is responsible for the provision and student selection instead of the Employment services. During independent studies, you are obliged to apply for and accept work, and participate in services promoting employment. 

You can receive unemployment benefits for short-term, part-time or full-time studies.

Short-term studies are studies that last for a maximum of six months. Short-term study with unemployment benefit is possible if you have not previously studied for a short period of time during the same unemployment.

Part-time studies are studies that are of minor scope or duration. Part-time studies may include, for instance, learning a new skill, completing basic studies at an open educational institution, or completing degree studies which have been previously interrupted. Full-time studies may also be part-time in some cases.

Full-time studies usually aim at completing a degree or other studies the extent of which is on average the minimum of 5 credits or 4.5 ECVET points per study month, or 25 hours a week. Full-time study with an unemployment benefit is possible if the Employment services estimates that you need education and that the studies significantly improve your chances of finding employment. The studies must have been agreed upon in the employment plan usually before starting the studies.
Short Description: During independent studies, you may receive unemployment benefits under certain conditions.
Other Links: Espoo Employment Services, office in Sello: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/76109; Espoo Employment Services, Piispanportti office: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/63889
Mini Description: An unemployment-benefit program that subsidizes self-directed independent studies—short-term, part-time, or full-time—for jobseekers who must actively seek work, participate in employment-promoting services, and follow an approved employment plan.

Description:
The start-up grant secures your livelihood during the establishment and consolidation stage of your business.

The start-up grant is discretionary support for a new entrepreneur. Its purpose is to secure an entrepreneur's livelihood at the starting phase of new full-time entrepreneurship when the income generated by the company is still low.

The start-up grant is granted for six months from the time you start as a full-time entrepreneur or expand your part-time business to full time. You may receive an extension to the start-up grant so that the total duration is no more than 12 months.

The start-up grant is equal in amount to a basic unemployment allowance. The start-up grant is paid for five days per calendar week.
Short Description: The start-up grant secures your livelihood during the establishment and consolidation stage of your business.

Public documents can be studied in the City Archives facilities and copies of them can be requested on site, by mail or by email. In the training trial, you can familiarise yourself with the studies at an educational institution and find out whether the field is suitable for you.

You can use the training trial to explore career choices and career options. The purpose of the trial is to determine whether the field and training are suitable for you. The training trial is organised at an educational institution and is planned individually according to your needs.

The training trial is agreed upon in the employment plan or other equivalent plan.

You will receive the same unemployment benefits during training trial as you do while you are unemployed. If you have agreed to a training trial in your employment plan or another plan replacing it, your unemployment security can be increased. This will be decided by the party paying the unemployment benefit - that is, by the unemployment fund or Kela. 

If the costs of participating in the training trial are incurred, you can receive expense allowance for the days of participation. If you do not receive expense allowance from the payer of the unemployment benefit, that is, an unemployment fund or Kela, the Employment services can pay a discretionary expense allowance.

Description:
You can use a work try-out to find out about career choices and career options in practical tasks. You can also use it to support your return to work.

A work try-out may be suitable for you if you are considering your own field or want to find out whether a field is suitable for you. A work try-out is also an option if you have been outside of employment for a long period. During the work try-out, you will participate in general work at the workplace. A work try-out is not an employment relationship, and it does not create expenses for the employer.

Agree on the duration and working hours of the work try-out together with the employment authority in your region and the employer. The maximum duration of a work try-out is six months. 

During the work try-out, you will receive the same unemployment security as if you were unemployed. If you have agreed to a work try-out in your employment plan or a plan replacing it, your unemployment security can be increased. This will be decided by the party paying the unemployment benefit - that is, by the unemployment fund or Kela. 

If the costs of participating in the work try-out are incurred, you can receive expense allowance for the days of participation. If you do not receive expense allowance from the payer of the unemployment benefit, that is, an unemployment fund or Kela, the Employment services can pay a discretionary expense allowance.
Short Description: You can use a work try-out to find out about career choices and career options in practical tasks. You can also use it to support your return to work.
Other Links: Espoo Employment Services, office in Sello: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/76109; Espoo Employment Services, Piispanportti office: https://www.espoo.fi/en/unit/63889
Mini Description: Work try-out is a temporary, non-employment work placement (up to six months) at a real workplace to explore career options and support a return to work, with unemployment benefits and potential expense allowances provided.

Service Name: building outside the town plan area
Description:
In Espoo, all areas that are not covered by the town plan are considered areas requiring planning. A building permit consists of examining preconditions related to area use (placement preconditions) as well as essential technical requirements (implementation preconditions). Building permits are granted by the municipal building control authority. By request of the permit application, the municipality can decide to resolve the existence of the placement preconditions by means of a separate decision (placement permit). Deviating from the rules, regulations, prohibitions and other restrictions stipulated in the Construction Act or adopted thereunder (for example, the regulations of the building code) is subject to a deviation permit.
